title: Don't Touch The Grass - thinking about co-op/multiplayer
author: lucasmonn
selftext:
Solo dev here. Made a short, cartoony precision platformer (Super Meat Boy-style: short stages, tight jump/dash, instant restart, par times for an A+ rank). Built in Godot, ported from a Three.js prototype.

Been toying with the idea of adding some kind of multiplayer

You can play it here: [https://lucasmon.itch.io/dont-touch-the-grass](https://lucasmon.itch.io/dont-touch-the-grass)

comments.author: MunchyCerealGuy
comments.body: Is there a reason the hazard is grass rather than something more instantly readable + culturally recognisable like lava or spikes?

replies.author: lucasmonn
replies.body: The idea for the game literally came to me when I read a sign that said "Keep off the grass" haha

comments.author: MunchyCerealGuy
comments.body:
Played it- the little character is great and the cartoon outline shader is really cute.

My one note: grass doesn't register as dangerous, so I don't understand why I was avoiding it. Either give it a consequence (an angry owner storms out to scold you?) or swap it for something with built-in stakes. Spikes and lava are the obvious picks but a bit overdone. Lego bricks, wet cement, Roombas are hazards that are less "this will kill you," and more like "everyone knows you don't step on that."

replies.author: lucasmonn
replies.body: You're right! I think I can solve this problem with the game's story and an "enemy" that monitors whether anyone steps on the grass, hahaha, but thank you very much for playing and for the feedback.

comments.author: visionode
comments.body: How much time to make the game?
